verdicts.rationale: In libs/payments/batch.py, replacing parallel authorization calls (asyncio.gather(*[authorize(i) for i in items])) with an async Batcher context manager (async with Batcher(**settings.payments_batch)) introduces batch collection delays and request serialization on payment gateway calls. This directly explains the p99 latency burn on POST /api/checkout/pay rising to 2.4s while 5xx error rates remain baseline.

In services/checkout/http.py, caching a single httpx.AsyncClient via @lru_cache def _shared_client() forces all checkout HTTP requests to share one client instance. Under high concurrency, default HTTP connection pool limits cause request queuing latency on outbound calls, contributing to elevated latency.

In deploy/checkout.yaml, increasing worker count from 8 to 16 could cause CPU context switching or resource contention, but is unlikely to be the primary cause of a 3x latency increase on POST /api/checkout/pay without causing errors.

Commit 311fb6d473 in libs/payments/batch.py replaces concurrent execution via `asyncio.gather(*[authorize(i) for i in items])` with `Batcher(**settings.payments_batch)`. Batching introduces wait windows and serialization overhead for payment gateway calls, directly explaining the p99 latency jump to 2.4s on POST /api/checkout/pay.

Commit 0a2edd8233 in services/checkout/http.py reuses a single `httpx.AsyncClient` via `@lru_cache`. Sharing a single AsyncClient across requests could cause connection pool contention or event-loop binding issues, though it is less directly tied to payment processing delays than the batching change.

Commit ee1837c66e in deploy/checkout.yaml increases checkout worker count from 8 to 16. Higher worker concurrency usually improves or maintains latency unless downstream dependencies are resource-constrained.

Commit 311fb6d473 in libs/payments/batch.py removed parallel execution via asyncio.gather(*[authorize(i) for i in items]) and replaced it with a Batcher context manager. Batching payment gateway calls per cart introduces batch window delays and sequential processing overhead during checkout, directly causing p99 latency on POST /api/checkout/pay to jump from 780ms to 2.4s while keeping error rates low (0.3%).

Commit 0a2edd8233 refactored services/checkout/http.py to reuse a shared httpx.AsyncClient via @lru_cache _shared_client(). Sharing an AsyncClient without proper pool sizing or lifecycle management can lead to connection pool contention and request queuing, contributing to latency spikes.

Commit ee1837c66e modified deploy/checkout.yaml to increase worker count from 8 to 16. While increasing concurrency can increase downstream lock contention, it is unlikely to be the primary cause of targeted payment latency degradation.

Dropping the old key invalidates all active sessions/tokens issued prior to rotation, directly causing POST /api/auth/verify to return 401 for 92% of requests across callers.

Commit 11788010d3 only modifies auth cache fetching and telemetry steps in services/auth/cache.py. It does not affect token verification logic or JWKS signing keys.
